blueprints.name: Northstar GRC
blueprints.tagline: Make controls, risks and evidence traceable.
blueprints.purpose: A governance workbench for maintaining a control library, tracking risk ownership, collecting audit evidence and reviewing compliance posture.
blueprints.audience: Compliance leads, internal auditors, risk owners and privacy or ESG teams.
blueprints.ux: A control-assurance cockpit: left-side framework rail, central control register with evidence freshness, and a right-side risk/evidence inspector. The primary interaction is evidence review and control attestation.
screens: Control register with owner, status and evidence freshness
Evidence review drawer with source and review notes
Risk register with inherent/residual score and treatment action
flows: Filter controls by framework, owner and assurance status.
Open a control and inspect the evidence bundle and review history.
Accept evidence, request a refresh or mark an exception.
Update a risk treatment and see the posture summary recalculate.
blueprints.model: Framework, Control, ControlTest, EvidenceItem, Risk, RiskTreatment, AuditEvent. Evidence records include provenance, collectedAt, reviewedAt and retention class.
blueprints.guard: Illustrative control catalogue only; do not claim certification or legal compliance. Do not include real personal data, sensitive evidence or actual audit findings. Seed demo controls and synthetic evidence.
prompts: Implement a versioned control library with framework mapping and control ownership.
Build an evidence review workflow with provenance, freshness windows and immutable audit events.
Add risk scoring and treatment tracking with deterministic test fixtures and audit-log tests.

blueprints.name: Blockscope Explorer
blueprints.tagline: Inspect blocks, transactions and contract activity.
blueprints.purpose: A read-only blockchain explorer prototype for searching seeded blocks, transactions, addresses and smart-contract events.
blueprints.audience: Developers, analysts and operators inspecting public chain activity.
blueprints.ux: A data-dense chain explorer with a live-feeling block ticker, searchable transaction ledger and right-hand detail inspector. The home view prioritizes chain health and block progression over wallet actions.
screens: Network overview with chain height and finality indicators
Transaction search and decoded event detail
flows: Search a seeded block, transaction hash or address label.
Select a block and inspect included transactions.
Open a transaction to inspect status, fees and event logs.
Filter contract events by event name and time range.
blueprints.model: Network, Block, Transaction, AddressLabel, Contract, EventLog, ValidatorSummary. Values are synthetic and explicitly labeled demo data.
blueprints.guard: Read-only explorer. No wallet connection, signing, transaction submission, token purchase, private keys or real financial advice. Do not imply the demo data reflects a live chain.
prompts: Create a typed read-only explorer domain model with block-to-transaction relationships.
Implement deterministic block, transaction and event search across seeded data.
Add transaction detail parsing, pagination and tests for pending, failed and finalized states.

blueprints.name: Federary Network
blueprints.tagline: See the shape and health of a federated network.
blueprints.purpose: A federation administration console for inspecting trusted instances, federation links, moderation queues and decentralized identity handshakes.
blueprints.audience: Operators of federated communities, decentralized services and self-hosted networks.
blueprints.ux: A network-first federation map with instance cards, trust edges and a moderation queue. Selecting a node opens its federation policy and peering history.
screens: Instance profile with software, policy and peer list
flows: Select an instance on the federation graph.
Inspect its published policy and peer relationships.
Review an incoming federation request or content report.
Approve, quarantine or block a peer using a reversible demo action.
blueprints.model: Instance, FederationLink, TrustRule, FederationEvent, ContentReport, ModerationDecision, IdentityAssertion.
blueprints.guard: Use fictional instances and synthetic identities. No deanonymization, scraping of real communities, impersonation or collection of sensitive personal data. Federation and trust actions are simulated.
prompts: Model federated instances, signed assertions and directional peer relationships.
Build a graph selection view with trust policy and peer status inspection.
Implement a moderation queue with reversible decisions and audit history tests.

blueprints.name: Swarmdrop
blueprints.tagline: Transfer large files through cooperating peers.
blueprints.purpose: A peer-to-peer transfer-room prototype showing peer discovery, chunk availability, transfer progress and integrity verification using synthetic local state.
blueprints.audience: Teams sharing large files, distributed compute groups and P2P product developers.
blueprints.ux: A transfer-first swarm console: large file manifest at the top, chunk map in the center, peer strip below and a live transfer event feed. It emphasizes how pieces move through the swarm.
screens: Chunk availability map and peer contribution
Peer details with latency and upload/download rate
Integrity verification and completed transfer receipt
flows: Create or join a seeded transfer room.
Inspect which peers have each file chunk.
Pause or resume the local transfer simulation.
Run integrity verification and inspect the completion receipt.
blueprints.model: TransferRoom, FileManifest, Chunk, Peer, PeerConnection, TransferSample, IntegrityCheck.
blueprints.guard: Simulation only: do not expose real IP addresses, create network sockets or transfer user files. Use synthetic peer IDs, synthetic rates and a fake share code.
prompts: Implement a deterministic chunk/peer availability model for seeded transfer rooms.
Build a peer contribution view that derives rates and progress from local fixtures.
Add pause/resume and integrity-verification states with edge-case tests.

blueprints.name: Strata CMS
blueprints.tagline: Structure content once. Publish it anywhere.
blueprints.purpose: A headless content management workbench for editing structured entries, managing collections, reviewing drafts and previewing channel output.
blueprints.audience: Content teams, editors, product marketers and developers building content-driven experiences.
blueprints.ux: A content studio with a collection rail, structured entry editor and live preview pane. The key interaction is editing schema-driven fields and switching preview channels.
screens: Collection overview with drafts and scheduled entries
Structured content editor with schema fields
Channel preview for web and mobile
flows: Choose a collection and open an entry.
Edit structured fields and inspect validation feedback.
Switch the preview between web and mobile renderings.
Submit the draft for review or publish the seeded demo entry.
blueprints.model: Collection, ContentType, FieldDefinition, Entry, Revision, Publication, ChannelPreview, EditorialReview.
blueprints.guard: Seeded fictional content only. Publishing actions update local demo state; there is no external CMS delivery, public posting or third-party API call.
prompts: Implement schema-driven content types with typed field definitions and validation.
Build a revision-aware entry editor with local web/mobile preview rendering.
Add editorial workflow states, publication scheduling and tests for required fields and revisions.

blueprints.name: Filewell
blueprints.tagline: Find, organize and understand your files.
blueprints.purpose: A desktop-style file manager prototype covering folder navigation, metadata, duplicate review, file conversion queue and synchronization status.
blueprints.audience: Knowledge workers and teams managing local project files and shared folders.
blueprints.ux: A dual-pane file manager with a navigable folder tree, dense file table, metadata inspector and a bottom action tray for organize/convert/sync operations.
flows: Navigate through the seeded project directory tree.
Select files and inspect metadata, versions and tags.
Review potential duplicates without deleting automatically.
Queue a demo conversion or synchronization task and inspect its status.
blueprints.model: FileNode, Folder, FileVersion, MetadataRecord, DuplicateCandidate, ConversionJob, SyncJob.
blueprints.guard: Never access the host filesystem. Use synthetic file entries and local-only demo actions. Duplicate cleanup is review-only and must not silently delete files.
prompts: Implement a virtual filesystem tree with stable node IDs and breadcrumb navigation.
Build metadata and duplicate-candidate services using seeded file fingerprints.
Add conversion/sync queues with cancel/retry states and tests that ensure no destructive default action.

blueprints.name: Musevault DAM
blueprints.tagline: Keep creative assets searchable, approved and licensed.
blueprints.purpose: A visual digital asset library for images, video, brand kits and campaign files, with metadata filters, rights windows and usage tracking.
blueprints.audience: Brand teams, creative studios, marketing departments and asset librarians.
blueprints.ux: An image-led masonry library with a left filter rail and a rich asset detail drawer. Rights and usage are first-class, distinct from ordinary file management.
screens: Visual asset library with collections and facets
Asset detail with metadata, tags and rendition previews
flows: Browse a seeded visual collection and filter by asset type or campaign.
Open an asset and inspect tags, rendition sizes and rights holder.
Review an expiring license and record a renewal reminder.
Inspect where an asset has been used and its approval status.
blueprints.model: Asset, Rendition, Collection, Tag, RightsRecord, LicenseWindow, UsageRecord, Approval.
blueprints.guard: Use generated or abstract visual placeholders and synthetic rights holders. No real copyrighted content, personal likeness or actual license claims. Rights status is sample data only.
prompts: Implement an asset catalog with faceted search, collections and rendition metadata.
Create a rights model with territory, permitted usage, expiry and reminder events.
Add approval and usage-history views with tests for expired and restricted assets.

blueprints.name: Identra Directory
blueprints.tagline: Manage the lifecycle behind every digital identity.
blueprints.purpose: An identity and access management console for directory users, groups, SSO applications, role assignments and joiner-mover-leaver lifecycle requests.
blueprints.audience: IT administrators, IAM teams and enterprise application owners.
blueprints.ux: An identity directory with a user-centric profile, group membership matrix and application assignment panel. The main workflow is identity lifecycle and authorization review, not sign-in.
screens: Identity profile with groups and attributes
flows: Search a seeded identity and open its profile.
Inspect group membership, roles and connected applications.
Review an access request and approve or deny the requested entitlement.
Simulate a joiner or leaver lifecycle action and inspect its audit trail.
blueprints.model: Identity, DirectoryGroup, Application, Role, Entitlement, AccessRequest, LifecycleEvent, AuditEvent.
blueprints.guard: Synthetic users only; no real directory connection, SSO provider, credentials or provisioning API. Never display real passwords, tokens or employee personal data.
prompts: Implement identity, group, application and entitlement models with explicit role relationships.
Build an access review workflow with least-privilege context and an auditable decision history.
Add deterministic joiner/mover/leaver simulations with tests for orphaned entitlements.

blueprints.name: Keyway Auth Lab
blueprints.tagline: Test the sign-in journey, not just the credential.
blueprints.purpose: A safe authentication UX lab demonstrating password, MFA, passwordless, passkey and hardware-key sign-in flows with risk signals and recovery states.
blueprints.audience: Product designers, application developers and security teams evaluating login experiences.
blueprints.ux: A split-screen sign-in simulator: selectable authentication method on the left, interactive device/verification ceremony in the center and a risk/explanation panel on the right.
flows: Choose an authentication method.
Complete the simulated challenge using clearly marked demo codes.
Inspect the session risk context and device trust explanation.
Try a recovery route and inspect the resulting authentication state.
blueprints.model: AuthMethod, AuthAttempt, Challenge, DeviceContext, RiskSignal, Session, RecoveryEvent.
blueprints.guard: No real authentication, password collection, biometric capture, passkey creation or hardware access. Use fake demo codes and fictional identities. Never present a demo sign-in as secure or production-ready.
prompts: Implement an authentication state machine for password, MFA, passkey and recovery demos.
Build risk explanations from synthetic device and attempt signals without opaque scoring claims.
Add scenario tests for successful, failed, expired and recovered authentication journeys.

blueprints.name: Cipherdesk
blueprints.tagline: Operate keys, certificates and signing workflows with care.
blueprints.purpose: A cryptographic operations workbench for reviewing key inventory metadata, certificate chains, signing requests and HSM/enclave status using synthetic fixtures.
blueprints.audience: Platform security engineers, PKI operators and teams managing certificate lifecycles.
blueprints.ux: A security operations console with a key-custody inventory, certificate-chain viewer and signing request queue. The interface focuses on lifecycle, ownership and auditability—not exposing key material.
screens: Key inventory with purpose, owner and rotation date
HSM / secure-enclave health and audit events
flows: Select a synthetic key record and inspect metadata and rotation status.
Open a certificate and inspect its parent/issuer chain.
Review a signing request and approve or reject the demo operation.
Inspect HSM health and a non-sensitive audit event trail.
blueprints.model: KeyRecord, KeyVersion, Certificate, CertificateAuthority, SigningRequest, HsmDevice, RotationEvent, CryptoAuditEvent.
blueprints.guard: No actual encryption keys, private key bytes, certificates trusted by browsers, signing operations, wallet secrets or cryptographic claims. All operations are simulated with clearly labeled placeholder material.
prompts: Implement key metadata and lifecycle models while ensuring secret material is never serialized to UI state.
Build a certificate-chain inspector with expiry and issuer relationships using synthetic certificates.
Add a signing-request queue and rotation policy simulator with tests for approval and expiry states.
